## Concise shortlist

### Starter pick — **Sainsbury’s Gluten-Free Roast Vegetable & Hazelnut Crumble**
**£2.58 per serving; serves 6; 1 hour 15 minutes; Easy.** It has butternut squash, celeriac, sweet potato and parsnip under a hazelnut/oat/parmesan crumble, with sage and nutmeg. This is the strongest choice for a small Christmas gathering: properly seasonal, cosy, vegetarian, and substantial enough to feel generous without competing with ham. I left its recipe page open.

### Gift pick — **Tommy Hilfiger Eau de Toilette Holiday Set (100ml) + Body Wash (100ml), Boots — £33**
A recognisably smarter, useful present rather than a novelty; the set combines fragrance with something he will use. Its Boots results page is left open.

### Gift pick — **Lacoste L.12.12 Blanc Gift Set: Eau de Toilette (50ml) + Shower Gel (100ml), Boots — £36**
The more polished fragrance-led alternative, still practical because it includes shower gel. Its Boots results page is left open.

## Sainsbury’s festive gluten-free starter options

1. **Gluten-Free Roast Vegetable & Hazelnut Crumble** — above. The recipe itself is explicitly gluten-free and uses gluten-free flour; use certified gluten-free oats if cross-contact is a concern.
2. **Taste the Difference Butternut Squash & Cranberry Wreath** — **£7, serves 4**, Food to Order. This is the most Christmas-looking ready-made vegetarian option: squash and cranberry make it a natural ham-menu contrast. **Important:** the Food to Order listing did not display dietary/allergen information in the readable page text, so check the product label/filter before relying on it for a coeliac guest.
3. **Taste the Difference Scottish Smoked Salmon & King Prawn Terrine** — **£17, serves 6**, Food to Order. Elegant, cold, and very manageable ahead of a ham main. Again, Sainsbury’s listing did not expose gluten status in the visible text, so confirm the label before purchase; serve with gluten-free crackers/bread rather than standard toast.

That is the practical mix I’d choose: cosy baked vegetable starter, showy vegetarian wreath, and an elegant chilled seafood option. Sainsbury’s own Free From page also explicitly advises checking packaging for specific dietary information.

## Ham: The Kitchn’s practical approach

The Kitchn’s comparison of six spiral-ham methods found its best moisture/flavour result came from cooking a bone-in spiral-cut ham **in an oven roasting bag at a low 250°F / about 120°C**. For your menu: use a fully cooked spiral ham, keep it enclosed in the bag for gentle reheating so the pre-cut slices do not dry out, then glaze near the end and serve it as the centrepiece. This is particularly host-friendly because the low, protected cook gives you headroom to finish the starter and sides rather than constantly tending the ham. The Kitchn article page itself blocked browser access, but I read the method summary in its search result.

## M&S stocking fillers under £20

- **M&S 5 Pack Cotton Rich Ribbed Socks — £14.** The best all-round dad choice: classic plain design, substantial yarn and a useful five-pack. I opened the product page; M&S describes them as flexible and comfortable for all-day wear.
- **Solutions for Men The Gym Edit — £16.** A practical grooming/active-lifestyle option, and less generic than novelty stocking fillers.
- **M&S Borg Slipper Socks — £12.** A cosy, useful Christmas-morning choice rather than clutter; listed on M&S’s Gifts for Him page with a 4.4 rating from 86 reviews.

## Two alternative Boots sets containing aftershave or body spray

- **Tommy Hilfiger Eau de Toilette Holiday Set 100ml + Body Wash 100ml — £33.**
- **Lacoste L.12.12 Blanc Gift Set, Eau de Toilette 50ml + Shower Gel 100ml — £36.**

For a lower-cost body-spray route, Boots also lists **Lynx Bodyspray + Bodywash + Towel Sunset Fresh & Epic Fresh Gift Set — £20**, though I would choose one of the two fragrance sets above for a more grown-up present.

Prices and availability can change; particularly for Christmas Food to Order, reconfirm collection date, stock and allergen information before ordering.

## Concise shortlist

### Starter pick — **Sainsbury’s Gluten-Free Roast Vegetable & Hazelnut Crumble**
**£2.58 per serving; serves 6; 1 hour 15 minutes; Easy.** It has butternut squash, celeriac, sweet potato and parsnip under a hazelnut/oat/parmesan crumble, with sage and nutmeg. This is the strongest choice for a small Christmas gathering: properly seasonal, cosy, vegetarian, and substantial enough to feel generous without competing with ham. I left its recipe page open.

### Gift pick — **Tommy Hilfiger Eau de Toilette Holiday Set (100ml) + Body Wash (100ml), Boots — £33**
A recognisably smarter, useful present rather than a novelty; the set combines fragrance with something he will use. Its Boots results page is left open.

### Gift pick — **Lacoste L.12.12 Blanc Gift Set: Eau de Toilette (50ml) + Shower Gel (100ml), Boots — £36**
The more polished fragrance-led alternative, still practical because it includes shower gel. Its Boots results page is left open.

## Sainsbury’s festive gluten-free starter options

1. **Gluten-Free Roast Vegetable & Hazelnut Crumble** — above. The recipe itself is explicitly gluten-free and uses gluten-free flour; use certified gluten-free oats if cross-contact is a concern.
2. **Taste the Difference Butternut Squash & Cranberry Wreath** — **£7, serves 4**, Food to Order. This is the most Christmas-looking ready-made vegetarian option: squash and cranberry make it a natural ham-menu contrast. **Important:** the Food to Order listing did not display dietary/allergen information in the readable page text, so check the product label/filter before relying on it for a coeliac guest.
3. **Taste the Difference Scottish Smoked Salmon & King Prawn Terrine** — **£17, serves 6**, Food to Order. Elegant, cold, and very manageable ahead of a ham main. Again, Sainsbury’s listing did not expose gluten status in the visible text, so confirm the label before purchase; serve with gluten-free crackers/bread rather than standard toast.

That is the practical mix I’d choose: cosy baked vegetable starter, showy vegetarian wreath, and an elegant chilled seafood option. Sainsbury’s own Free From page also explicitly advises checking packaging for specific dietary information.

## Ham: The Kitchn’s practical approach

The Kitchn’s comparison of six spiral-ham methods found its best moisture/flavour result came from cooking a bone-in spiral-cut ham **in an oven roasting bag at a low 250°F / about 120°C**. For your menu: use a fully cooked spiral ham, keep it enclosed in the bag for gentle reheating so the pre-cut slices do not dry out, then glaze near the end and serve it as the centrepiece. This is particularly host-friendly because the low, protected cook gives you headroom to finish the starter and sides rather than constantly tending the ham. The Kitchn article page itself blocked browser access, but I read the method summary in its search result.

## M&S stocking fillers under £20

- **M&S 5 Pack Cotton Rich Ribbed Socks — £14.** The best all-round dad choice: classic plain design, substantial yarn and a useful five-pack. I opened the product page; M&S describes them as flexible and comfortable for all-day wear.
- **Solutions for Men The Gym Edit — £16.** A practical grooming/active-lifestyle option, and less generic than novelty stocking fillers.
- **M&S Borg Slipper Socks — £12.** A cosy, useful Christmas-morning choice rather than clutter; listed on M&S’s Gifts for Him page with a 4.4 rating from 86 reviews.

## Two alternative Boots sets containing aftershave or body spray

- **Tommy Hilfiger Eau de Toilette Holiday Set 100ml + Body Wash 100ml — £33.**
- **Lacoste L.12.12 Blanc Gift Set, Eau de Toilette 50ml + Shower Gel 100ml — £36.**

For a lower-cost body-spray route, Boots also lists **Lynx Bodyspray + Bodywash + Towel Sunset Fresh & Epic Fresh Gift Set — £20**, though I would choose one of the two fragrance sets above for a more grown-up present.

Prices and availability can change; particularly for Christmas Food to Order, reconfirm collection date, stock and allergen information before ordering.
